hero.headline: Bringing Devotion Home
hero.subtext: Authentic pooja essentials, divine idols, brass collections & spiritual decor — curated by artisans, delivered with care to your sacred space.

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.importance: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu, marking the triumph of dharma over adharma.
festivals.poojaVidhi: A midnight abhishekam is performed for the Bala Krishna idol with milk, curd, honey, and tulsi, followed by aarti and prasad distribution.
festivals.origin: Observed on the Ashtami of Krishna Paksha in Bhadrapada month, marking Krishna's birth in Mathura over 5,000 years ago.

festivals.name: Navaratri
festivals.importance: Nine nights honoring the nine forms of Goddess Durga, celebrating the victory of good over evil.
festivals.poojaVidhi: Kalash sthapana on day one, followed by daily alankaram of the goddess and Golu doll displays, culminating in Vijayadashami.
festivals.origin: Rooted in the legend of Durga's battle with the demon Mahishasura across nine nights.

festivals.name: Deepavali
festivals.importance: The festival of lights celebrating Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya and Goddess Lakshmi's blessings of prosperity.
festivals.poojaVidhi: Lakshmi-Ganesha puja performed at dusk with diyas lit around the home, followed by exchange of sweets.
festivals.origin: Marks Rama's homecoming after 14 years of exile and the victory of light over darkness.

articles.title: How to Choose the Right Krishna Idol for Your Home
articles.excerpt: A guide to selecting the ideal material, size and posture for your home altar.
articles.body: Choosing a Krishna idol depends on your altar space, the material (brass, panchaloha, or marble), and the posture — standing, seated, or with flute. Brass idols are easiest to maintain with daily abhishekam, while panchaloha idols are prized for ritual worship. Consider the idol's gaze direction and proportion to your altar before purchasing.

articles.title: Importance of Kumkum in Daily Pooja
articles.excerpt: Understanding the spiritual and cultural significance of kumkum in Hindu worship.
articles.body: Kumkum, made from turmeric and lime, symbolizes auspiciousness and is applied during daily worship, festivals and rites of passage. Its red hue is associated with Goddess Lakshmi and vitality, and applying it to the deity's forehead is considered essential in most household pooja routines.

articles.title: Vastu Tips for Pooja Room & Sacred Spaces
articles.excerpt: Simple placement principles to bring positive energy to your prayer space.
articles.body: The pooja room ideally faces east or northeast, keeping idols away from the bathroom or bedroom walls. Lamps should be lit facing east, and the room should remain clutter-free with fresh flowers replaced regularly for optimal energy flow.

articles.title: Complete Guide for Varamahalakshmi Pooja
articles.excerpt: Everything you need — from the kalash setup to the concluding aarti.
articles.body: Varamahalakshmi Pooja is performed on the Friday before the full moon in Shravana month. It begins with kalash sthapana representing the goddess, followed by decorating with a silk saree, offering fruits and sweets, and concluding with an elaborate aarti and distribution of prasad and gifts to married women.
